# Oracle Database

Oracle's relational database engine. Used in exactly one repository in this source set:
[[oracle-database-laboratories]], targeting **12c or later** — XE (the free Express Edition) is
explicitly stated as sufficient — driven entirely through [[sql-plus]] scripts.

## What the repo actually exercises

Oracle-specific features, in the sense that a port to another engine would need rework:

| Area | Feature |
|---|---|
| Hierarchy | `CONNECT BY PRIOR`, `LEVEL`, `SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH`, `CONNECT_BY_ROOT` — see [[hierarchical-queries]] |
| Reshaping | `PIVOT` |
| Top-N | `ROWNUM`, and the 12c row-limiting clause `FETCH FIRST … ROWS WITH TIES` |
| Nulls | `NVL` (Oracle's `COALESCE` predecessor, still idiomatic here) |
| Sets | `MINUS` — Oracle's spelling of `EXCEPT` |
| Dates | `MONTHS_BETWEEN`, `ADD_MONTHS`, `SYSDATE`, `EXTRACT`, `TO_CHAR` |
| Identity | `SEQUENCE`, and `GENERATED BY DEFAULT ON NULL AS IDENTITY` (12c) |
| Procedural | packages, compound triggers, `PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION` — see [[plsql]] |
| Objects | `CREATE TYPE … AS OBJECT`, typed tables, `REF`/`SCOPE FOR`/`DEREF` — see [[object-relational-model]] |
| Merge | `MERGE`, used to close a check-then-write race in a trigger |

## Version-sensitive details worth remembering

- **`FETCH FIRST … WITH TIES` is 12c+.** Before that, Top-N is an inline view plus `ROWNUM`, and the
  repo writes both so the older form stays readable.
- **`ROWNUM` is assigned before `ORDER BY` runs.** `WHERE ROWNUM = 1 ORDER BY col DESC` does not
  return the largest row — it returns whatever the access path emitted first, then sorts that one row.
  The fix is to force the sort to complete in an inner query block first.
- **`RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR` accepts only -20000 to -20999.** Any other code raises ORA-21000
  instead of the intended message.
- **`GENERATED … AS IDENTITY` is 12c+**; earlier schemas need a sequence plus a trigger, which is why
  both idioms appear in the same file.
- **Constraint names are unique per schema, not per table** — which is why the object-relational lab
  suffixes every constraint to coexist with the relational schema.

## NLS is the portability hazard

Several traps in the repo are the same trap: an implicit conversion routed through the session's
`NLS_DATE_FORMAT`. Comparing a `DATE` column against a bare string works on a session set to
`YYYY-MM-DD` and raises ORA-01861 on any other; concatenating a `DATE` onto a string produces
different text per session. The repo's answer throughout is ANSI `DATE '2009-01-01'` literals and
explicit `TO_CHAR` with a stated mask — a script that carries its own formatting assumptions instead
of inheriting them.

## Operational surface not exercised

No tablespace management, no partitioning, no `EXPLAIN PLAN` or optimiser hints, no RAC, no Data Pump,
no execution statistics. Cost arguments in the repo are made in prose (a query per cell versus one
aggregating pass, a sort avoided by `UNION ALL`) rather than measured. Compare [[sqlite]] and
[[neo4j]], the other two engines in this source set, both used with far less of their surface but
with the same script-first discipline.
